value: Brain activation related to choosing the valuable (vs. devalued) response in the non-cued condition, over and above brain activity related to choosing these valuable (vs. devalued) responses when these are elicited by the cues, was observed in the posterior vmPFC. This suggests that the vmPFC tracks action values in the absence of a cue but not when the response is elicited by a Pavlovian cue.
The observed increase in posterior vmPFC activity to responses associated with valued outcomes was specific for the non-cued trials and was absent in cued trials.

spans.text: In other words, our interaction analysis probed for neural responses that track the action values in the absence of a cue while not being involved in tracking these action values in the presence of a cue (involving S→O→R associations). Pavlovian-instrumental transfer (PIT) task

description.value: A modified combined PIT/outcome-devaluation paradigm involving instrumental and Pavlovian training, satiation, and non-cued and cued test trials.

spans.text: The study consisted of instrumental and Pavlovian training phases and a satiation manipulation outside the scanner (Fig. 1 A) followed by a test phase inside the scanner (Fig. 1 C).
non-cued trials
During the non-cued trials, we assessed choice behavior in the absence of Pavlovian cues

description.value: During non-cued test trials, participants responded freely by pressing either food-associated key during a 3-second purple-box availability period while the background changed to a checkerboard with flipped colors and no Pavlovian cue was presented. Responses were recorded to assess value-directed, goal-directed choice between the valued and devalued outcomes.

spans.text: cued trials
During the cued trials, we assessed whether presentation of the different Pavlovian cues would bias responding on different keys

description.value: During cued test trials, participants responded freely by pressing either food-associated key during a 3-second purple-box availability period while one of the food-associated Pavlovian background patterns was presented. The cue signaled popcorn or Smarties, and responses were assessed as compatible or incompatible with the signaled outcome to measure outcome-specific Pavlovian-instrumental transfer.

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to learn which response key produced popcorn or Smarties, attend to the Pavlovian cue–outcome relationships, and during the test phase press either key as often as they liked during 3-second availability periods to win food outcomes. They were told that only one outcome was available on each trial, that outcomes would not be revealed after each test trial, and that they should primarily focus on the purple response box while occasionally seeing patterned cues.

stimuli.value: Images of popcorn and chocolate Smarties; a purple response-availability box; black-and-white patterned Pavlovian cues; a no-outcome cue followed by the word “nothing”; checkerboard backgrounds; fixation cross; and feedback words/images during training and query trials.
